items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I’d like you to come in and see what kind of rapport — and I’d like you to be musical director... So now I became not a little kid anymore, I became the musical director of the Regis show.

ctx.x: Well this is sort of a two part question. I wonder if you had definite goals for a life in music and did your mother support them? Did she think you were going into the right career?

Well it started like I never had goals. I never had goals. And I’ve been blessed things fell in my lap. I never would have auditioned with Benny Goodman, he called me. I never auditioned with Woody Herman, he called me. I never auditioned with Steve Allen, Regis Philbin, they called me. So I’ve been blessed in that way, and I never had goals. I wanted to play good. That was my goal if anything, I just wanted to play to where I enjoyed it. I never, you know it’s wild to say I never play for an audience. I play for…
Okay yes that’s — I’m going to catch a plan out there and get that.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And so the Regis Philbin Show... I was the second banana... we got along great.

ctx.x: How did you get to know him?

Well I got to know him, he was a fan of mine. [pause for refreshment] That’s right keep bringing ‘em in. Stop putting all that vodka in this. I quit drinking years ago. I thank you very much. He was a fan of mine. He used to come, in New York, when I played Birdland. He’d come in all the time to hear me. And when I moved out to California he’d come in to see me playing all the time. And I moved back to New York for almost a year and I got called, he was doing a television show and I got called — he quit the show…

a question, “yes,” “no,” he asked him. Finally I said, “Regis, I want to ask Basie a question.” He said, “Go ahead, Terry.” I went down and said, “Basie, when we played in Detroit that time, remember that scene with Pee Wee Marquette? Tell Regis.” He had to tell the story now. So every time we had a jazz musician — Stan Getz, every time he interviewed, I had to be down there with him. He was really great. That wasn’t his bag. I used to put him on all the time. He always thought that we were putting him on because…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I gave him the Steve Allen and Regis Philbins and Don Rickles and the Milton Berles, and all the things I had something to do with my television experience.

ctx.x: And the first chapter has been sent in. I gave them the television chapter because they know I’m a jazz musician, there’ll be a lot about jazz musicians, and I gave him the Steve Allen and Regis Philbins and Don Rickles and the Milton Berles, and all the things I had something to do with my television experience. So they liked it. Now when I get back, I’m writing with a gentleman called Cary Ginell, who produced an NPR show, a Nancy Wilson thing, for my 75th birthday. And he’s editing the thing with me. So we…
names. But I can talk about it now. Because I look for humor in everything. Things that weren’t funny then, I can look now and they were funny but tragic at the same time.
